Formulation
- Predisposing: Past history of asthma and hay fever (atopic background).
- Precipitating: Recent travel to the United States with increased walking; transient sore throat and a posterior calf rash noted ~end February.
- Perpetuating: Ongoing uninvestigated symptoms for ~6 weeks, reduced exercise, reduced appetite and daytime tiredness affecting activity and concentration.
- Protective: Supportive spouse, patient engaged with care and consenting to investigations and telephone follow-up.
- Summary: A previously well adult developed persistent fatigue, generalized aching and reduced concentration over ~6 weeks following travel; a transient calf rash and sore throat around the same time raise concern for possible tick-borne or other infectious causes (Lyme disease mentioned). Plan focuses on targeted blood investigations and telephone follow-up to determine further management.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Persistent fatigue, generalized aching, reduced energy (~6 weeks); possible Lyme or other infectious cause.
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Return to baseline energy levels and activity/exercise routine.
  - Improve concentration and work effectiveness.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Exclude common medical causes of prolonged fatigue (including FBC, liver and renal function) and specifically test for Lyme disease/tick-borne infection.
  - Provide appropriate treatment if investigations identify a specific cause (e.g., antibiotics if Lyme serology positive).
- Actions (Patient):
  - Book and attend recommended blood tests via the support line as advised.
  - Arrange telephone follow-up approximately one week after tests are completed.
  - Monitor symptoms and report any new/worsening signs (e.g., persistent fever, new rash, marked functional decline).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange blood investigations as discussed: full blood count, liver function tests, renal function (kidney tests), and Lyme serology (and other relevant blood tests as clinically indicated).
  - Review blood results when available and discuss results with patient by telephone follow-up (~1 week after tests).
  - If Lyme serology positive, arrange appropriate antibiotic treatment per local guidance.
  - Consider further medical referrals if tests are abnormal or symptoms persist.

Secondary Problem: Reduced concentration and decreased exercise/physical activity.
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve concentration at work and gradually resume usual exercise levels.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Support symptomatic recovery and safe graded return to exercise/work as medically appropriate.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attempt graded activity as tolerated; prioritize rest and pacing until cause identified.
  - Continue to attend work where feasible and notify employer if function deteriorates.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide advice about pacing and graded return to activity.
  - Reassess work capacity after investigations; consider referral (e.g., to occupational health or relevant specialty) if prolonged impairment.

- Education Given: Yes.
  - Topics Covered: explanation of need for blood tests to check liver/kidney function and blood count; possible Lyme disease/tick-borne infection as a potential cause of rash and systemic symptoms; treatment available if Lyme positive; plan for follow-up.
